scope: isolated local macOS native QA; metadata-only evidence; no production change
question: Can the matched eighteen-skill native snapshot expose a bounded AI resource-value class without retaining card identities or private state?

qaPackage.manifestRevisionNote: The isolated QA manifest retains the expected 40-hex revision for the runner; packageSha256 identifies the actual staged tree, which includes the captured working-tree QA init.lua change.

resourceValue.definition: A coarse class derived from the real AI keep_value valuation for selected resource cards: none means no selected resource card, low is a summed value at or below 30, medium is above 30 and at or below 45, high is above 45, and unknown means the value could not be safely classified.

sourceChanges.purpose: Emit a sanitized coarse keep_value resource class from the real native player.ai:makeReply() result without retaining exact card values or identities.
Parse optional resource_value metadata, compare bounded bucket changes, and expose availability without retaining native IDs or private state.
Verify unknown legacy traces and known resource-value traces remain compatible and compare correctly.

verification.officialPairedParser: 3/3 pairs parsed; all status MATCHED_NATIVE_SKILLS with zero request-state mismatch
verification.candidateNativeRuns: 3/3 EXIT 0; fixed four-seat native trace reached GameOver
verification.baselineNativeRuns: 3/3 EXIT 0; fixed four-seat native trace reached GameOver
verification.resourceValueAvailability: 54/54 candidate and 54/54 baseline decisions classified without unknown

limitations: The baseline intentionally disables the selected Prompt 4 strategies; reply and resource-bucket deltas are expected behavior deltas, not causal proof of improved gameplay or win rate.
The resource_value field is a coarse AI keep_value class for selected resource cards. It is not an exact resource cost, tactical value, downstream-effect result, or win-rate metric.
none includes replies with no selected resource card and does not distinguish every skill-specific reason for not spending a card.

The pair gate proves bounded request-state equality using sanitized fingerprints and matching native handler metadata; it is not a full engine-state serialization or an exhaustive opportunity denominator.
Three seeds and one declared roster matrix are not a population sample; aggregate request safety outside the fixture, full-game/reconnect/device, release/rollback and canary gates remain open.
No raw logs, card/target IDs, private hands/generals, prompts, credentials, exact keep_value numbers or exception payloads are stored in this artifact.
